title: Control Plane init + scale sanity checks and Terraform snippets
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a field-oriented runbook for initial commissioning of a Private Control Plane (VPC or on-prem), the basic scaling sanity checks we run during the first week of traffic, and a compact set of Terraform module snippets and upgrade/rotation play sequences.

Audience: field engineers doing first-time customer installs and SREs running early-life support. This is deliberately concise — use it as a checklist + quick reference. Longer design docs and TF module source live in infra-private repo.

1) Quick preflight (15–30m)
- Confirm access: customer KVM/console and VPN or jumpbox credentials are working.
- Inventory: collect instance types, NICs, attached storage IDs, and GPU types (if Dedicated or inference edge is colocated). Write these to the customer onboarding ticket.
- Secrets: verify KMS/Cloud HSM connectivity; do NOT rotate keys before cutover. Ensure service account principals listed in the onboarding doc exist.
- Network: confirm CIDR allocations, peering/VPC routes, and firewall rules for control-plane pods (API server, controllers, etcd) and telemetry endpoints.
- Time sync: ensure NTP/chrony is running across nodes. Certificate validity has bitten us before when clocks drift.

2) Bootstrap sequence (expected runtime: 30–90m)
- 0. Prepare a temp admin kubeconfig with short-lived certs for operator actions.
- 1. Apply TF to provision base infra: vpc, subnets, route tables, base instances. Use `terraform apply -target=module.network -auto-approve` for incremental.
- 2. Populate secrets into KMS/secret store (do not commit values to state). Use `vault write` or cloud KMS workflows per customer.
- 3. Init and seed etcd (on baremetal clusters we use a quorum of 3). Validate with `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://x:2379 endpoint status`.
- 4. Bring up operator pods and controllers. Check `kubectl -n redwood get pods` and wait for `READY 1/1` for core pods.
- 5. Run smoke requests against the control plane REST endpoint: auth token handshake, simple model list call, and a health endpoint.

3) Minimal Terraform snippets (paste-friendly)
- network module sample (variable-driven):
```
module "private_vpc" {
  source = "git::git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-private.git//modules/vpc?ref=stable-2025-03"
  name = var.cluster_name
  cidr = var.cidr
  public_subnets = var.public_subnets
  private_subnets = var.private_subnets
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { "redwood:env" = var.env })
}
```
- controlplane nodes (autoscaling group style, on-prem uses provisioning_count):
```
module "cp_nodes" {
  source = "git::git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-private.git//modules/controlplane-nodes"
  count = var.cp_count
  instance_type = var.cp_instance_type
  labels = { role = "control-plane" }
}
```
Notes: avoid putting long-lived credentials in TF variables. Prefer reference to secret manager resources. Keep state in remote backend with locking enabled.

4) Scale sanity checks (scale up and scale down sequences)
- Reason to scale: CPU saturation on controller loops, etcd pressure (compaction lag), or growth in agent telemetry.
- Safe scale up: increase `cp_count` by 1 (for clouds) or provision a new node image and join for on-prem. Run `kubectl get cs` and `kubectl top nodes` before and after; observe controller-manager and scheduler CPU for 15–30 minutes.
- Safe scale down: drain node with `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Wait for control-plane components to re-elect and re-sync. Do not drain more than one control-plane node in 24 hours for small clusters (<5 cp nodes).
- Post-scale validation: run a set of smoke tests (see repo/test/smoke) covering API list, create/update/delete, and a few synthetic inference queries through the hosted gateway.

5) Rotation/upgrade plan (operator, PKI, KMS, and TF state)
- Goals: non-disruptive, reversible steps. Have a rollback snapshot for etcd and a tfstate backup before each major step.
- Operator binary upgrade: apply rollout in canary mode. Patch operator deployment with new image tag and watch leader election. If leader restarts fail >3x, rollback image.
- Certificate rotation:
  - Prepare new CA certs on a staging path; do not overwrite live until all nodes accept them.
  - Use `cert-manager` sequence: issue new certs, update API server flags, and roll API server pods one at a time. Validate client handshake using `openssl s_client`.
- KMS/HSM key rotation: schedule with customer; ensure all secrets referencing old key have a transition path. Test decrypt with both old and new key (if supported) before retiring old key.
- Terraform changes: always run `terraform plan` and review diffs in PR. For changes that modify instance_type or subnet attachments, expect a node replacement window. Create a rolling plan: `terraform apply -target=module.cp_nodes -parallelism=1` for node-replacing changes.

6) Rollback recipes (fastest recovery)
- Broken control-plane after upgrade: restore etcd from snapshot taken immediately before the upgrade. Steps: stop API server, restore etcd (follow etcdctl restore flow), start API server, verify endpoints.
- Failed TF apply: `terraform state pull` to get current state; if drift introduced destructive changes, revert to the tfstate snapshot from pre-apply and re-run.
- Operator misbehaviour: scale operator replicas to 0, revert image, scale back up.

7) Observability checks during early-life (first 72h)
- Dashboards to monitor: cp-latencies, etcd_ops/sec, controller-event-rate, pod-eviction-rate, API-server request latencies (P50/P95/P99).
- Added probe: a scheduled job that performs a 3-request inference chain every 5m and records token-level latency. This has high signal for regressions post-upgrade.

8) Runbook snippets (commands to copy)
- Check API server health:
  kubectl get --raw='/readyz' -s https://<apiserver>:6443 --insecure-skip-tls-verify
- Etcd endpoint list:
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.0.5:2379 member list --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/etcd.crt --key=/etc/etcd/etcd.key
- Taking etcd snapshot (hot):
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://10.0.0.5:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/etcd.crt --key=/etc/etcd/etcd.key

9) Shortform troubleshooting guide
- Symptom: API server 503s after operator upgrade
  - Check `kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/operator -p` -> look for schema migration errors.
  - Check etcd health and compaction lag. If compaction backlog is high, restore snapshot.

- Symptom: slow token generation for hosted gateway
  - Check redis/memcache hit rates, check prefix cache logs on serving runtime, and confirm KV cache warming state.

10) Open items / TODOs
- Add an automated TF dry-run check in CI to catch provider behavior changes (PR: infra-private#310).
- Document exact safe window for CP node maintenance when customer telemetry is >500 req/s.
- Put together a small test harness that simulates certificate rotation end-to-end in CI.

11) Lessons from recent installs (ops notes)
- On-prem disks: prefer multipath configs and explicit fstab entries — we had two installs where nodes failed to reattach local volumes after reimage.
- Rolling etcd compactions: schedule compaction after low-traffic windows; compaction-induced CPU spikes on small nodes can cascade.
- TF provider versions: pin the provider in module root. A provider auto-upgrade during `terraform init` caused a subtle subnet diff for one customer.

Contacts / Escalation
- On-call SRE: pager link in ticket (internal)
- Private deploys lead: Anya Petrov (anya@redwood.ai)
- Infra module owner: Marcus Lee (marcus@redwood.ai)

Appendix: quick checklist (one-liner)
- [ ] Preflight network & keys
- [ ] TF base network applied
- [ ] Etcd quorum seeded and snapshot taken
- [ ] Operator pods up and healthy
- [ ] Smoke inference queries passed
- [ ] TF state backup stored
- [ ] Observability alerts baseline recorded

End of runbook — file serves as an on-the-ground reference and should be iterated after each field install. If you modify TF snippets here, open a PR against infra-private and crosslink the PR in linked_artifacts.
